title: Dasakam 4
description: Bhattathiri contemplates the practice of yoga, liberation, and refuge in the Lord.

source.status: unreviewed source captions; Sanskrit and translation pending

stanzas.commentary_en: Narayana Bhattathiri requested Bhagwan Guruvayoorappan to give him enough of adequate good health to practice Ashtanga yoga and earn HIS grace.

The practice of Ashtanga yoga include self control (Yama) by practice of brahmacharya, follow a code of conduct (Niyama) like taking bath & attain purity of body and mind by sitting in an appropriate posture (Asana) like Padmasana or Sukhasana to meditate upon Bhagwan.

Bhattathiri continues that by regulating breath through Pranayama and having purified, he will continuously chant the Pranava (Om) mantra mentally and withdraw his senses from the sense objects (Pratyahara), and prepare himself for meditation on Bhagwan.

After attaining the above, Bhattathiri would try hard to fix his mind (Dharana)on the lotus feet of the hazily perceived form of Bhagwan. Practicing again and again he shall attain bliss of devotion and tenderness of heart.
With prolonged meditation (Dhyana) and surrender, he would then be successful in visualising Bhagwan’s form more clearly in an effortless manner.
Having been captivated by Bhagwan’s sweet form (Saguna), he would then be able to enjoy the impersonal form of Bhagwan which is Parabrahman or the Nirguna form.
While practicing such a nirvikalpa Samadhi state, if Bhattathiri missed his focus, he would start from the meditation process, Dhaarana onwards.

Thus having attained the joy of experiencing the Supreme Blissful state, Bhattathiri requests Bhagwan to make him the foremost of the liberated devotees and move about freely like Sri Shuka, Naradha and others.

After one achieves this Samaadhi state, he can opt for immediate liberation (Sadhyo Mukthi) or gradual liberation (Krama Mukthi). In both ways, one should first control the breath by Pranayama and then make it arise from the Mooladhara chakra to higher six chakras through the Sushumna naadi.

One who is not interested in heavenly worlds, gives up his gross and subtle body and merges with Bhagwan through the Aajnya chakra. One who desires to visit heavenly worlds, before attaining liberation, then leaves his breath through the Brahmarandra or through the orifice in the crown of the head.

Bhagwan’s devotee who follows the Krama Mukti path is led by the presiding deities of fire, day time, the bright fortnight, and Uttaraayana to the plane of the sun and enjoys in each of these spheres & reaches the realm of Dhruva.

Reaching the abode of Dhruva, he proceeds to Maharloka. When, at the approach of cosmic dissolution, fire emanates from the mouth of Aadishesh, and when he is tormented by the fire, he takes refuge in Bhagwan and goes to Brahmaloka.
The devotee residing in Brahma loka or Bhagwan’s Vaikunta is then liberated during Mahapralaya or if he desires, even much earlier by liberating himself with his yogic powers.

The liberated devotee enters each of the seven sheaths of the cosmic sphere,i.e. earth, water, fire, air, space, the cosmic intelligence, and primordial nature. He enjoys the bliss there and then merges with Bhagwan, the Supreme Brahman.

The devotee who thus goes through the luminous path does not fall any more to the netherworlds. Bhattathiri worships the embodiment of pure consciousness absolute, to protect him who  ever sings  Bhagwan’s glories.
